---
title: "Day 1 / Morning: Extra examples"
---

## Order of operations

1. Simplify: $\frac{18-4}{2}+3(5-2)^2$

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
$$
\frac{18-4}{2}+3(5-2)^2 = \frac{14}{2}+3(3)^2 = 7+3(9) = 7+27 = 34
$$
:::

2. Simplify: $2x+5(3x-4)-\frac{6x}{2}$

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
$$
2x+5(3x-4)-\frac{6x}{2} = 2x+15x-20-3x = 14x-20
$$
:::

## Solving equations

3. Solve for $x$: $5x-7=3x+9$

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
$$
5x-7=3x+9 \Rightarrow 2x=16 \Rightarrow x=8
$$
:::

4. Solve for $x$: $3(2x-1)=5-(x+4)$

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
$$
3(2x-1)=5-(x+4) \Rightarrow 6x-3=1-x \Rightarrow 7x=4 \Rightarrow x=\frac{4}{7}
$$
:::

## Rules of exponents

5. Simplify: $\frac{5^7}{5^4}$

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
$$
\frac{5^7}{5^4} = 5^{7-4} = 5^3 = 125
$$
:::

6. Simplify: $(2x^3y^{-2})^3$

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
$$
(2x^3y^{-2})^3 = 2^3x^{9}y^{-6} = \frac{8x^9}{y^6}
$$
:::

7. Simplify: $\frac{x^4\cdot x^2}{x^6}$

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
$$
\frac{x^4\cdot x^2}{x^6} = \frac{x^{4+2}}{x^6} = \frac{x^6}{x^6} = x^0 = 1
$$
:::

8. Simplify: $\left(\frac{2x}{y}\right)^3$

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
$$
\left(\frac{2x}{y}\right)^3 = \frac{2^3x^3}{y^3} = \frac{8x^3}{y^3}
$$
:::

9. Evaluate: $27^{2/3}$

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
$$
27^{2/3} = \left(27^{1/3}\right)^2 = 3^2 = 9
$$
:::

## FOIL & polynomials

10. Expand: $(3x-2)(x+4)$

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
$$
(3x-2)(x+4) = 3x^2+12x-2x-8 = 3x^2+10x-8
$$
:::

11. What is the degree of the polynomial $4x^5-3x^2+7x-1$, and how many terms does it have?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
The degree is **5** (the largest exponent), and the polynomial has **4 terms**.
:::

## Unit conversions

12. Convert 15 miles to kilometers, given 1 mile = 1.609 km.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
$$
15\text{ mi} \times \frac{1.609\text{ km}}{1\text{ mi}} = 24.135\text{ km}
$$
:::

13. Convert $250\ \frac{mg}{L}$ to $\frac{g}{m^3}$, given 1000 mg = 1 g and 1 L = 0.001 m^3^.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
$$
250\frac{\text{mg}}{\text{L}} \times \frac{1\text{ g}}{1000\text{ mg}} \times \frac{1\text{ L}}{0.001\text{ m}^3} = 250\frac{\text{g}}{\text{m}^3}
$$
:::
